title: ReadPosition bidirectional note references only account-level receiptSharing, not Chat-level override
description:
Location: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md, ReadPosition section, line ~763.

The bidirectionality note reads: 'when PresenceStatus.receiptSharing is false, the server MUST NOT deliver inbound Peer/receipt events (carrying readAt) to the owner's clients.' This references only the account-level PresenceStatus.receiptSharing field.

However, Chat.receiptSharing (line ~441) is defined as a per-chat override that takes precedence over the account-level setting. If Chat.receiptSharing is false for a specific Chat (while PresenceStatus.receiptSharing is true), the bidirectionality property should equally apply for that Chat. The current wording implies it does not — an account with a per-chat override of receiptSharing=false would still receive inbound Peer/receipt events for that Chat.

Additionally, the bidirectionality note is in the ReadPosition section but does not address the Chat-scoped case at all, leaving an incomplete picture of when inbound receipts are suppressed.

Correct behavior: The bidirectionality note (and/or the Receiver Behavior in federation-00.md) MUST be updated to cover the effective preference (Chat.receiptSharing if present, else PresenceStatus.receiptSharing), not just the account-level field.
close_reason: Fixed: ReadPosition bidirectional note now covers both account-level and per-Chat override (chat-00.md:763)
